clue.text: Part of our capital accordingly goes on house

parts.note: so means accordingly, therefore
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A remark that a slice of the capital is set aside for housing, as if from a planning report.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a district in central London, the 'our capital' of a British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a well-known district of London's West End, so it is one part of the British capital.

clue.text: Number crossing river, one that rises in Wales

indicators.note: something crossing another lies across it, so one word straddles and encloses the other

parts.note: a number, chosen to fit
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tally of people crossing a river, one of whom stands up in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rises' is the misleading word: a river rises at its source, and the Severn's is in the Welsh hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn, Britain's longest river, has its source on Plynlimon in mid-Wales before flowing into England.

clue.text: Group of soldiers out of ammunition

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the following word, sitting inside it unchanged

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word, after its first three

explanation.surface: A squad of soldiers that has run out of bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit is an organised body of troops, such as a company or battalion.

clue.text: Crazy artists in Indian city now recalled

parts.note: mad means crazy
an RA is a Royal Academician, so artists are RAs

explanation.surface: Wild painters in an Indian city that people still remember.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now recalled' looks like memory; it means the city's old name survives only in memory, since Madras was renamed Chennai in 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Madras is the former name of Chennai, so it is an Indian city whose name is now only remembered.

clue.text: Upheld agreement to marry, after wife's demonstrated subservience

indicators.note: after places the marrying part second, behind the wife's letter, though the clue names it first
in a down entry, holding something up turns it to read from the bottom upward

parts.note: OK signals agreement
W is the abbreviation for wife; the 's means 'has' here, the next part following
TO kept as written, then WED for marry

explanation.surface: A wife's acceptance of a marriage proposal, upheld, shows she was meek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the to-marry part after the wife's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To kowtow is to kneel and bow submissively, so having kowtowed means having shown servile deference.

clue.text: Son belatedly changed deadline for retailer

indicators.note: changed tells us the preceding letters are rearranged into a different order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A son, too late, moves a shop's deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-by date is the date stamped on goods after which a shop should no longer offer them.

clue.text: House upset with MP, new and unsophisticated

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The House of Commons is in uproar over a fresh, rather naive member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' tempts you to write HOME; it is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun originally meant cloth spun at home, hence plain and simple, lacking polish or sophistication.

clue.text: Reading's certainly held up by friend

indicators.note: a thing held by another is gripped inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: sure means certainly

explanation.surface: The town of Reading is definitely being delayed by a mate.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the Berkshire town; it is the act of reading, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a reading of something, especially a careful or thorough read-through.

clue.text: Declared a verse outstanding

parts.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for verse
a debt that is outstanding is still owed

explanation.surface: Someone announced that a particular poem was excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as praise; here it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to state openly, so avowed means openly declared or acknowledged.

clue.text: Problem around university affected fellow

indicators.note: one thing placed around another wraps it, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A difficulty at university has hit one of its fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected fellow' reads like a don hit by a problem; affected here means pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur is a person who behaves affectedly to impress others, a show-off with pretensions.

clue.text: Choke or other part of engine

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the valve controlling fuel flow, a different part from the choke

explanation.walkthrough: The choke is itself part of an engine, so 'other part' cleverly points to a neighbouring component while 'Choke' is really the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle is to strangle; the throttle is the valve regulating fuel or air into an engine.

clue.text: Sight on coast castaway genius in distress

indicators.note: things in distress are troubled and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brilliant shipwrecked sailor is seen struggling on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The Giant's Causeway is a field of basalt columns on the Northern Ireland coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Giant's Causeway is a famous tourist attraction of interlocking basalt columns on the County Antrim shoreline.

clue.text: One or two, very unusually, found in academics' dwelling

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters before it come in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: One or two oddballs, notably, turn up in university lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is a figurative refuge of intellectuals, a state of privileged seclusion from practical life.

clue.text: Announced place in church for convert

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we want a word sounding like the phrase that follows

parts.note: the altar is the communion table in a church

explanation.surface: A church spot is publicly named as the venue for a religious conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' reads as a new believer in the church scene, but it is the verb meaning to change.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change it, the same as converting it into a different form.

clue.text: Give orders to leaders in band of savages, say

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters, so we take the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Instructions given to chiefs of a tribe of wild warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: To boss someone is to order them around in a domineering way.

clue.text: Reminder of place over in US that's been transformed

indicators.note: something transformed has changed shape, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A memento of a spot back in America that has changed beyond recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a keepsake bought or kept to remember a place visited.

clue.text: Section of novel — it hopefully is in print

indicators.note: a section is a portion cut from within, so the letters run continuously inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word across the second into the third

explanation.surface: An author hopes an extract of their novel will be published.
explanation.definitionFit: A litho, short for lithograph, is a print made by the lithographic process.

clue.text: Like final man to leave, survive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words, dismissed at the end, like the last batsman out
second meaning: to live or last longer than

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the answer into two words; in cricket the last batsman is out last.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast someone is to survive them, lasting longer; split, it describes being out in the final position.

clue.text: Play stopped early for wee drink

indicators.note: stopped early means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A theatre show halted before the end so the audience can have a little tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' is Scots for small, apt for a whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small measure of spirits, especially Scotch whisky.

clue.text: Child actor as exiled prince

parts.note: young as a noun means offspring, a child
an actor pretends, so is a pretender

explanation.surface: A child performer is cast as a banished prince.
explanation.walkthrough: The Young Pretender was Charles Edward Stuart, Bonnie Prince Charlie, claimant to the British throne who died in exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie Prince Charlie, called the Young Pretender, led the 1745 rising and spent his later life abroad in exile.

clue.text: Good parties providing wine from Bordeaux

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
raves are lively dance parties

explanation.surface: Fine celebrations serving French claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a wine district of Bordeaux, and its red and white wines bear the name.

clue.text: Switch position after somebody else produces idea

indicators.note: after sends the switch setting second, behind the other person, though the clue names it first

parts.note: somebody else is not me, read as 'not I'
on is one of the two positions of a switch

explanation.surface: Changing jobs to follow another person sparks a thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch position' reads as changing jobs; it is a setting on a light switch. 'After' puts it behind the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief, synonymous with an idea.

clue.text: Supporting English players, made prediction

parts.note: being for something means supporting it
E is the abbreviation for English
the cast is the set of players in a show

explanation.surface: A fan backing the England team called the result in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to predict, and the past tense means having made a prediction.

clue.text: Out of pity, person's kind

indicators.note: the letters come out of the following words, running straight across them

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Someone acting from compassion is a kind person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' reads as the adjective for a pitying person; it is the noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a category or sort, the noun sense of kind.

clue.text: Engaged in change of course in storm

parts.note: at, as in 'at work', means engaged in
a sailing boat tacks to change course

explanation.surface: A sailor busy altering direction during a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' sits in the sailing scene as weather but is the verb, as in storming a fort.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it suddenly and violently.

clue.text: In speech, philosopher is unable to use specialised language

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken out loud, so we want a word sounding like the clue words

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was the German philosopher

explanation.surface: A spoken complaint that a thinker cannot handle jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the philosopher and the contraction meaning 'is unable' sound identical, so the phrase 'Kant can't' doubles the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To cant is to talk in the jargon of a particular group, cant being its specialised vocabulary.

clue.text: Western half of very pleasant World Heritage Site

indicators.note: in an across entry the western side is the left, so we keep the first half of the following word

parts.note: the first two of this word's four letters
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Part of a truly delightful protected landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice and its lagoon are listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

clue.text: Lacking room to grow, best put back before spring

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: top means best
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: A cramped gardener's advice: best plant the seedlings out ahead of springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' tempts as the season beside 'grow'; it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-bound plant has roots filling its container, so it has no space left to grow.
